text:
ana: heads up — during the last regional failover we saw a short spike in 5xxs and our egress NATs exhausted ephemeral ports for ~45s. geo-dash shows a big jump in new outbound connections from eu1 -> internet. any thoughts? :eyes:

jp: saw it. eu1 nat-gw metrics spiked, ephemeral_used -> 98% then we hit connection failures. service-level 429/503s from downstream.

sre-bot: incident: nat-port-exhaustion detected on nat-gw-aws-eu1 (alert_id: NAT-EXH-2026-03). automated mitigation: scale-out attempt triggered.

michael: TL;DR: geo-dns TTL=20s + aggressive probe policy caused clients to flip quickly between old/new egress IPs, creating a burst of new connections and exhausting the ephemeral port space. we should stop immediate flip behavior and add smoothing.

lina: can we pre-warm SNAT or add an egress proxy to multiplex connections? pre-warm would reduce peak new ports. also consider keepalive tweaks on LBs.

jp: also noticed our geo-failover policy marks region down on a single probe failure (super sensitive). that makes the whole population re-resolve at once. change to consecutive_failures = 3 and add a grace_window.

ana: (replying) proposed config changes: set geo DNS TTL -> 60s, probe_threshold -> 3 consecutive failures, failover_grace -> 90s, and add 5-15s randomized jitter before switching to new region. also add a nat_port_utilization alert at 75%.

ops-oncall: I can own the small roll tonight. what exact commands/queries do you want me to run?

michael: runbook snippets below — add to ops playbook.
```
# quick checks
dig +short api.redwood.internal @ns-geo1 || true
# expect: one A record (primary) and one A record (fallback) during transition
# view nat usage (cloud provider metric placeholder)
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace "Network/NAT" --metric-name "EphemeralPortUsage" --dimensions Name=NatGateway,Value=nat-gw-aws-eu1 --start-time 2026-03-17T00:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-17T01:00:00Z --period 60 --statistics Average
# update route53 TTL (example change)
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZZ --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.internal.","Type":"A","TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"1.2.3.4"}]}}]}'
```

lina: for pre-warm we can add a tiny fleet of always-open long-lived connections from eu1 to the providers, or enable socket_reuse on our egress proxies. also LB keepalive to 120s helps.

jp: I'll add dashboard and alerts: metric nat_ephemeral_utilization (region) and alert at 0.75 sustained for 1m, and an anomaly alert for sudden delta > 30% within 30s.

ama: summarizing action items:
- ana: run staging test of new TTL/probe settings and validate no thrash (owner)
- jp: update dashboards + alerts (owner)
- michael: write runbook steps and CLI snippets into runbook doc (owner)
- lina: prototype nat pre-warm and keepalive changes (owner)
- ops-oncall: be standby for 6pm small roll

ana: let's not forget to document the behavioral expectation in the runbook so sales/CS don't get surprised by short blips during the change.

ops-oncall: ok I'll schedule the deploy and ping here when done. :thumbsup:

michael: one more note — if we add jitter, prefer randomized delay at DNS resolver TTL boundary, not immediate client-side backoff (harder to enforce).

jp: monitoring checklist for rollout: region nat port % chart, 5xx rate, DNS query rates, number of distinct egress IPs returned.

ana: thanks all — will post status updates here during the roll. :hammer_and_wrench:
